g.text: Home Depot is also in the MRO business, with a surprisingly
different take on organization and promotions than Grainger.
• Header links include: DIY Projects, Pro Xtra, Order Status,
Sign In, Cart, and a Search Field.
• The navigation is open by default on the landing page
and broken up into two sections, categories & misc.
• More than half of the page is dedicated to promotions.
• Followed by the top ten selling categories
• Two more promotions follow below that.
• Categories and sub-categories are clearly displayed
and abundant, with both as jumping-off points.
• Static promotional section at the top of the page
• Subcategories (ranked by popularity), with images follow
• The left-rail is also a list of sub-categories along

EVERYTHING YOU NEED TO UPDATE YOUR BATH
Lowes' search is basic, with a few touches to help in the process.
• Type ahead is broken out into two sections,
• Thumbnail images are used for quicker identification.
• The search field is visually distinctive from
• Results are shown in List View by default.
• A tab is given as a quick ability to see what
• The left-hand rail is shown for filtering.

A few promotions are more helpful than none.
Discounts may not be the key selling points to getting
users to purchase items, once on your site. Organizing
products into collections that ring familiar allow users
to more quickly / easily understand the necessity.
Categories should be easy and quick to navigate
Major categories / collections should be visible at all times,
with a sub-category fly-out optional. Possible rework of
category titles. More IA work needs to be done to find if
this is feasible and worth executing.
Filtering is appropriate, at the right times (levels).
Introducing the ability to filter is a powerful way to streamline
results. Although, with questionable taxonomy, it may become
more of a hinderance than a help. The key is to get the user
down far enough in the browse path to make filters reliable.
Attributes should be limited to the top 5-6 with
Listing out all possible attributes by default can lead to
left-rail blindness. An overwhelming amount of choices often-
times distracts the user to not make any decision.
The quicker you can add to a cart, the better.
Adding the ability to add to your cart in a results view makes
sense when enough information is made available to make
Offer related search terms, products and other
pieces of information on result pages.
Show "related" search terms and other "related" products
at various points of the search and browse experience.
A major concern is that the current amount of items in
the left-hand navigation push sections of the menu
below the fold. A regrouping exercise may help in shortening.
If Product Pages start getting long in length,
consider floating menus with anchor points.
Alleviate scroll-fatigue by offering the user a quick way
to jump from section to section without traveling too much.
Consider adding the ability to select Paint Color
Ability to select the color choice from the Result List will
save users time with not having to click into the choice.
Consider pulling the top three filtering attributes
from the left-rail into an impromptu table header.
Users can sometimes lose sight of specific attributes in
the left-rail. Pulling out 2-3 of the most used filters
may greatly increase Result List functionality.
